capabilities: Toggle a fullscreen Zen mode for the active tab
Hide panels, icons, scrollbar, header and graph controls
Dim the screen edges with an adjustable vignette
Center text content regardless of the Readable line width setting
Configure a content fade-in animation on entering Zen mode
extras: Not yet in the community plugin gallery; manual installation from release files is described. A known issue resets Zen mode styling on pane cycling or graph view switching.
motivation: The author, a tech writer, built it for his own daily use: 'describing this stuff requires full concentration on fine wording. So, ProZen is what I made for myself to use on daily basis.'
problem: Obsidian shows multiple panels, tabs and controls that distract from concentrated writing or reading, and there is no true fullscreen distraction-free mode.
summary: Zen mode that expands the active tab to fullscreen, hiding all panels, icons and scrollbar, with optional vignette dimming for focused reading and writing.
